Dear Dr. Morrison,

Thank you for agreeing to consult on this 21-day-old male infant, born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, who has been admitted to our care unit since delivery. 

The infant presented with congenital fluid overload, displaying diffuse bodily anasarca from his first day of life. Bloodwork confirmed strikingly depressed serum albumin concentrations alongside heavy urinary protein loss. His metabolic panels demonstrate severe, terminal-stage functional renal impairment corresponding to stage 5 renal insufficiency. A postnatal renal ultrasound demonstrated poor demarcation between the renal cortex and medullary pyramids.

Physical examination reveals a head circumference falling dramatically beneath the third percentile, accompanied by a notably constricted bitemporal width. Craniofacial features include widely separated eyes, a flattened nasal bridge, and a markedly diminutive, retropositioned lower jaw. Upon intraoral inspection, a midline fissure of the palate is evident. His ears are unusually large and sit noticeably low on his head. Furthermore, brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an exceptionally small cerebral volume coupled with an abnormally smooth, agyric cortical mantle.

His cardiopulmonary examination is benign, with normal peripheral pulses, regular rate, and clear breath sounds bilaterally. Abdominal palpation reveals no hepatosplenomegaly. Family history is non-contributory; his parents are non-consanguineous and his older sister is thriving. He is currently tolerating specialized feeds via nasogastric tube and receiving cautious fluid management.

We would be very grateful for your comprehensive clinical assessment and recommendations regarding his ongoing care.

Sincerely,
Dr. Eleanor Vance
